index.summary: Define the first iteration-first XML and XPath core.

product.objective: Deliver a local XML and XPath workflow that lets an Agent discover an Iteration, read compact Task indexes, load one complete Task, and update Task state atomically.

index.summary: An Iteration-first filesystem layout without project.xml.

deliverable.description: Date-prefixed Iteration directories expose project work through one ordinary directory listing.

index.summary: Composable XPath variables and structural projection.

deliverable.description: The query engine supports variables, ds:filter, ds:filter-out, and compact XML results without silent truncation.
A transaction command updates tasks.xml without persisting claim or completion transaction documents.

included.item: Product, design, Task, record, and reference XML structure.
XPath 1.0 variables and structural projection extensions.

excluded.item: MCP, GUI, schedulers, signatures, and audit hash chains.

index.summary: Agents discover Iterations through date-prefixed directories.

requirement.statement: A directory named YYYYMMDD-name containing spec.xml is an Iteration. Its spec root ID must equal the directory name.
requirement.rationale: Filesystem discovery must remain understandable before an Agent loads a project catalog or learns the complete XML model.

index.summary: Agents can query compact Task indexes before Task content.

requirement.statement: ds:filter and ds:filter-out operate on each selected element's direct attributes and direct child elements and return composable node sets.
requirement.rationale: Index-first projection prevents large Task bodies and record history from consuming context during routine navigation.

index.summary: Structured records preserve resumable reasoning and history.

requirement.statement: Discussions, alternatives, attempts, decisions, blockers, verification, and completion remain with the owning context instead of separate Evidence or transaction files.
requirement.rationale: A conclusion without its trigger, alternatives, and reasoning is difficult for a later Agent to trust or safely revise.

key_points.point: Preserve the reasoning needed to avoid repeating the discussion.
Persist structured summaries rather than complete chat transcripts.

index.summary: Decided how much discussion history must be retained.

record.summary: Reviewed whether durable state should retain only conclusions, complete transcripts, or structured reasoning summaries.
record.context: Later maintainers may not understand a conclusion when the motivating problem and rejected alternatives have disappeared.

option.reason: It loses the reasoning needed for later revision.
It adds noise and unbounded context cost.

option.summary: Persist trigger, options, reasons, and outcome.
option.reason: It preserves understanding with bounded content.

record.outcome: Requirements and Tasks may carry structured discussion records; product conclusions still require explicit confirmation.

index.summary: Template-first Task updates remain revision-checked and atomic.

requirement.statement: An Agent obtains a schema-valid template, fills it, and uses append or Task update helpers. The generic transaction remains an escape hatch.
requirement.rationale: Raw transaction XPath and ordered operations are too error-prone for routine append-oriented history and Task state changes.

key_points.point: Prefer a readable schema-valid template over memorized transaction operations.
Preserve the generic transaction only for unsupported combinations.

index.summary: Selected template-first append for routine mutations.

record.summary: Compared raw transaction requests with schema templates and append-oriented helpers.
record.context: Most durable updates append records, while raw transactions make the caller repeat paths, XPath, cardinality, and operation order.

option.summary: Use raw transactions for every mutation.
option.reason: Routine writes have excessive cognitive and error cost.

option.summary: Add one CLI command for every Task transition.
option.reason: It expands the surface without improving record shape.

option.summary: Fill schema templates and append or atomically update.
option.reason: It keeps XML visible while removing low-level mechanics.

record.outcome: V1 exposes template show, append, and Task update. Transaction apply remains available but is not the normal Skill path.

acceptance.criterion: One directory listing reveals Iterations and special project content.
A new Agent can select the first unfinished Task and load its complete durable context without loading other Task bodies.
Task verification and completion provenance are recorded inside Task records without a required Evidence document.
Query result limits fail explicitly and never silently truncate XML.
A later Agent can recover the trigger, material alternatives, rationale, and outcome of an important Requirement or Task discussion.
An Agent can obtain a schema-valid template and perform a routine append or Task update without authoring a raw transaction.

design.overview: The filesystem is the coarse project index. spec.xml owns product and design intent. tasks.xml owns implementation state and semantic execution records. XPath provides narrow reads inside either document.

boundaries.boundary: The nearest ancestor .dogdouspec directory is the project boundary.
One date-prefixed directory is the ownership boundary for one Iteration.
Transaction requests are execution inputs, not persisted project state.

index.summary: Use the filesystem as the project-level Iteration index.

decision.rationale: Directory names expose time, topic, and available work before an Agent understands any project XML schema.

index.summary: Keep product and design separate from mutable Task state.

decision.rationale: spec.xml changes when product or design meaning changes. tasks.xml can change frequently while retaining small and reviewable Git diffs.

index.summary: Record ordinary verification inside the owning Task.

decision.rationale: Most verification is meaningful only in the context of the Task and does not require an independent evidence lifecycle.

index.summary: Persist bounded structured reasoning, not conclusions alone.

decision.rationale: Trigger, options, rejection reasons, and outcome preserve long-term understanding without retaining a complete conversation transcript.

index.summary: Use schema templates and append-oriented helpers by default.

decision.rationale: Templates keep XML explicit while helpers own revision checks, selection cardinality, timestamps, and atomic Task state updates.

confirmation.summary: Product scope, acceptance criteria, and design were reviewed and approved for implementation.
Approved structured reasoning records and template-first append/update as the v1 design baseline.
